articles.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
articles.summary: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. articles.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
articles.summary: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. articles.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
articles.summary: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator. On AlpacaEval 2.0 with GPT-4o as judge, three iterations raise the length-controlled (LC) win rate against GPT-4o from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral, and the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct on every reported win rate. With same-family open-weight annotators, the runs retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of the LC gain achieved with GPT-4o as annotator, so the rating step does not require a proprietary model. articles.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
articles.summary: Undesired model behaviors can emerge or re-emerge at any stage of training. Once observed, how effectively can we suppress them? To study this question, we first construct two model organisms--language models deliberately trained to exhibit a specific misalignment--that differ in what triggers the behavior. The narrow-trigger organism misbehaves only when the prompt contains a specific cue: it cheats on multiple-choice questions by following a planted hint that points to a wrong answer, and behaves normally otherwise. The broad-trigger organism has no such cue: after fine-tuning on insecure code, it gives harmful responses across a wide range of open-ended prompts. We then formalize post-hoc behavioral suppression and evaluate methods along three criteria: immediate suppression of the target behavior, durability under further training, and preservation of general capability. articles.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
articles.summary: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). articles.summary: Speculative decoding has been treated purely as a systems optimization that speeds up large language model decoding without changing the model behavior. Under this view, the growing effort to train better draft models has been focused solely on acceptance rate. We argue that this view does not hold true for long-horizon agent reasoning. Measuring frontier open-weight models on complex agentic tasks with different speculative decoding approaches, we found that numerical noise grows within verification windows, and the draft acceptance results of the thinking process can change the output distribution of the model after 30 steps, thus noticeably influencing the reasoning accuracy of long-horizon agents in random directions. While we cannot change the overall token distribution verified by the target model, we can encode critical reasoning with highest precision by training the draft model to be rejected. articles.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
articles.summary: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass. Prior work found candidate parts but not how they compose. We give the composition for few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels in three 3-4B-parameter transformers. The model implements a key-value memory over label-token positions: each label token's residual stream encodes the label's identity, and middle-layer attention heads write into it the class of the preceding demonstration as its key. At the query, upper-layer heads match the query's class against the stored keys and copy out the matching labels. An early-layer signal encoding whether any label has repeated gates this readout; in its absence the readers attend to the start of the prompt and no label is favored. A separate set of heads suppresses the most recently seen label. articles.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
articles.summary: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data. Frontier language models have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of small neural networks, an ability called weight-space programming. The purpose of this study was to determine whether such a model, given only a clinical protocol and a network's weights, can audit and repair the network. Networks with 433 to 4,801 parameters were trained to screen head-and-neck planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through the training data: confounds that hid each rule, a 3 Gy shift in the cord threshold, and a hidden trigger. Claude Opus 5.5 audited each network blind, without tools, data or code execution, and every claim and repair was tested on about 420,000 requests. rights.modified: 仅收录标题、时间与原始链接；未收录正文

editorial.lead:
概述：据 IT之家报道，松下电器机电宣布向 AI 相关业务投入 920 亿日元，涉及多层基板材料、电容器产能和下一代半导体封装材料研发。项目包含分期投产安排，尚不能理解为新增产能已经全部释放。

核心要点：

2. 日本宇治与印尼峇淡的 SP-Cap 电容器项目计划合计投入约 170 亿日元，面向 GPU 等 AI 服务器元件的中长期需求。
3. 四日市的新研发大楼计划投入约 80 亿日元，重点是下一代半导体封装材料；这些均为公司公布的建设和投资计划。

articles.title: 《纽约时报》等媒体起诉浏览器公司 Brave，指控其未经授权抓取版权内容并转售给 AI 公司

rights.modified: 仅收录标题、时间与原始链接；未收录正文

editorial.lead:
概述：据 IT之家报道，《纽约时报》等出版商在曼哈顿联邦法院起诉 Brave，指控其未经授权抓取受版权保护的内容并提供给 AI 企业。报道介绍的是原告的指控与诉求，不代表法院已认定侵权。

核心要点：
1. 《纽约时报》以及《每日新闻》《芝加哥论坛报》《奥兰多哨兵报》分别提起诉讼，争议集中在网页抓取、索引和向第三方提供内容。
2. 诉状还涉及付费墙访问及广告经营行为；指控中提到的索引规模和商业行为，需要结合答辩及后续审理判断。
3. 原告请求禁令和损害赔偿。当前报道不能被解读为已有判决，也不能把原告的指控直接当作查明事实。

articles.title: Anthropic 警示：AI 递归自我改进（RSI）近在眼前

rights.modified: 仅收录标题、时间与原始链接；未收录正文

editorial.lead:
概述：据 IT之家对 Anthropic 招股补充文件的报道，公司认为 AI 辅助研发可能加快模型能力提升，使安全与对齐措施的开发难以同步。文件同时明确：当时没有现有模型越过其定义的相关递归自我改进门槛。

核心要点：
1. “可能很快触及”的判断基于内部测算及对下一代模型的预期，并不是已经实现递归自我改进的公开证明。
2. 公司将研发加速视为机会与风险并存的问题，计划通过《负责任扩缩策略》监测和缓释风险。
3. 文件表示，未来开发仍需有效的人类监督；媒体标题中的“近在眼前”不应替代文件对现有模型状态的限定。
